newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil grants rubber-tappers extractive reserve.
newsitem.headline: Brazil grants rubber-tappers extractive reserve.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Tuesday granted rubber-tappers a special jungle reserve area in a bid to help them survive in the face of cheap rubber imports from abroad.

Atanagildo Matos, head of the National Rubber-Tappers Council (CNS), told reporters after meeting President Fernando Henrique Cardoso that Brasilia would hand over 1.85 million acres (750,000 hectares) of Amazon jungle to producers of natural rubber.

Matos said Cardoso had guaranteed natural rubber would get a "minimum price" in the Brazilian market, taking into account the environmental benefits of farming for rubber extracts. He gave no details.
The CNS won the concession from Brasilia after about 200 rubber-tappers came to the Brazilian capital on Monday demanding support for natural rubber production.
The CNS says its members earn a miserly $30 a month on average, far below Brazil's official $108 monthly minimum wage, and cannot compete against Asian imported rubber without protection.

Brazilian rubber tappers entered the world spotlight with the assassination of their leader, rainforest champion Chico Mendes, in 1988. Mendes was gunned down by cattle ranchers in the Amazon after leading a campaign against land clearing and in support of the rubber-tappers' traditional way of life.
